theorem: For initialized, current-parameter RTL control traces compatible with the reviewed legal single-beat read-only fixture memory, coordinator k_a_valid implies k_a_ready at sampled non-cold-reset cycles.
method: Compositional inference from independently checked component induction/combinational results plus exact source clock/reset, phase, parameter and handshake bindings; not a new monolithic formal run.
temporal_argument: Initial cold reset puts coordinator in NORMAL, so AS assertion is vacuous before recovery.
Successful DRAIN establishes authority quiet from actual drained/retired/abort aggregation.
Phases1..9 have no admin/AP offer; with quiet, AP-owned is absent and authority request is absent outside AS. Independent quiet/no-fault persistence preserves Q until first AS.
In AS, independently established configured/admin/AP exclusions and Q satisfy the unconditional combinational sufficient-ready lemma, yielding ready without assuming AS=>ready as an input contract.
AS may consume the request and become AW, where Q is not asserted. A successful AW response is the exact authority response handshake; local retirement re-establishes Q on entry to OS.
OS/OW/NEXT preserve Q with no authority request, including correction/deferred/retry paths to subsequent AS. Failures cannot jump directly to AS; new attempts return through DRAIN.
The checked conditional history induction establishes these state invariants; its four assumptions are supplied by the independent binding and component reviews, including configured qualification.
noncircularity: Q history relies on DRAIN/response retirement and request/admin exclusion, configured relies on metadata/retirement/persistence; neither is derived from KA readiness. Only the final sufficient-ready implication uses Q/configured.
limitations: Two-state RTL/control theorem at current parameters and legal fixture memory, not arbitrary AXI, all parameters, four-state gate equivalence, timing or board behavior.
